quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #3
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Which of these substances can impair your driving and result in a DUII arrest?
questions.explanation: Many substances can impair your driving. These include alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many prescription and over-the-counter medicines.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, you should:

options.text: Be ready to react to road hazards.

questions.explanation: Stay alert on highways and be ready to react to dangers. Keep your eyes moving to avoid highway hypnosis. Do not look at one thing for more than a few seconds.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to keep right to avoid a hazard ahead. Drivers must follow the rules on regulation signs.

questions.question: Where can drivers not park?
questions.explanation: You cannot park on a bridge, overpass, underpass, or in a tunnel.

questions.question: If you see this sign, you:

options.text: May pass a slow vehicle if you do it quickly.
May pass if you know the road ahead.
May pass, but only at night.

questions.explanation: This white rectangular sign is a regulatory sign. Drivers must obey it. Where this sign is posted, you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: To be safe at a railroad crossing, you should:

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains from both directions. Watch for signals of an approaching train. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: Drinking alcohol and driving is:

options.text: Safe if you have had only a few drinks.

questions.explanation: Drinking and driving is a serious safety problem. Safe driving is not possible with alcohol or drugs in your system. It is dangerous to you and to others on the road.

questions.question: Before entering a roundabout, you must slow down and yield to:
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by:

options.text: All passengers every time the car is driven.

questions.correctAnswerText: All passengers every time the car is driven.
questions.explanation: Everyone in your vehicle should wear a seat belt every time. In a crash, a person without a seat belt becomes a dangerous projectile.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: You must change your driving when weather changes suddenly.
Slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Be aware of vehicles behind you in bad weather.

questions.explanation: Adjust your driving when weather changes. Slow down in rain and fog. Be alert for vehicles behind you that may be going too fast for conditions.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing, what should you do?
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing sign, slow down, look for a train, and be ready to stop. If red warning lights are flashing or the gate is down, you must stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol?

options.text: They are always aware of the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
They are better drivers because they drive more carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their body, mind, or vehicle properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain and body. It harms your judgment, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What happens when you mix alcohol and drugs?

options.text: The effects of drugs and alcohol decrease.
The effects of both drugs and alcohol increase.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects of both drugs and alcohol increase.
questions.explanation: Mixing alcohol and drugs can make the effects of both stronger. It is unsafe to drive after consuming alcohol or drugs alone. It is even more dangerous to combine them.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a roundabout is coming. Enter the roundabout at a slow speed and let traffic already in the roundabout go first.

questions.question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention to the road
Driving too fast for the conditions

questions.explanation: Driving too fast for conditions causes many crashes. Not paying attention can cause you to hit other vehicles. Following too closely causes most rear-end collisions.

questions.question: What is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: They drive slower than normal traffic.
They make quick and sudden stops.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include speeding, weaving between lanes, driving slower than traffic, making jerky movements, and making quick stops.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing. You do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: When a stop sign is posted.
When a crossing gate is down.
When the crossing lights are flashing.

questions.explanation: Always stop before the tracks if flashing red lights are on, the gate is down, a stop sign is posted, someone signals you to stop, or a train is close. When in doubt, stop. Never try to race a train.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop or back up on the highway, cross multiple lanes at the last second, or turn around across the median. These actions are illegal and very dangerous.

questions.question: North Dakota law says you must use headlights:

options.text: During the day in good weather.

questions.explanation: North Dakota law requires you to use headlights between sunset and sunrise. Use low beams when within 500 feet of an oncoming car. Also use low beams when following another vehicle within 300 feet.

questions.question: A driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that this driver is not paying full attention and is less safe.

questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, looking for things, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming while driving. If a driver near you is not paying attention, give them extra space because accidents are more likely.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
Do what other cars are doing, even if the crossing guard says otherwise.
Assume the guard should not be directing traffic.
Follow the normal rules as if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the crossing guard tells you to do.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful when a sign, crossing guard, or police officer tells you to. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Look carefully for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: When you see a yellow traffic light, you should:

options.text: Speed up to avoid hitting a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right of way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what the cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming next. Stop unless you are already crossing through the intersection.

questions.question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:

options.text: Check your rearview and side mirrors.
Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal early, check both mirrors, and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: You are driving on a divided multilane highway and see or hear an emergency vehicle. You should:

options.text: Ignore it if other lanes are open for the emergency vehicle.
Stop as fast as you can.
Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, move to the side to clear a path, and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights, slow down, move aside to create space, and stop. Do not try to outrun the emergency vehicle.
